# HomePowerRebate

HomePowerRebate helps homeowners across Canada and the United States find every home-energy rebate they qualify for — heat pump, solar, battery storage, insulation, water heater, windows, EV charger, and smart thermostat programs — and connects them with vetted local installers they choose themselves. Programs differ by province, state, and even utility territory; we calculate the real stacked total for each specific city rather than a national average.

## What we do

- Calculate the exact rebate stack (government + utility + federal, where still active) for a homeowner's specific city
- Rank every covered city by PowerScore, a 0-100 score of how generous and accessible its rebate stack actually is (see /powerscore/)
- Run a Stacking Calculator that shows how multiple rebates combine for one home (see /stacking-calculator/)
- List real local installers per city and category, sourced from Google Places (ratings, review counts, contact info) — homeowners browse and choose, we do not route exclusive leads to a single installer
- Publish independent guides and blog content on rebate programs, retrofit sequencing, and equipment comparisons
- Flag when programs have closed, changed, or been replaced — we do not show stale rebate amounts as current

## Regions covered (18)

**Canada**
- Ontario — Home Renovation Savings pays up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump that replaces electric, oil or propane heat. 25 cities, including Toronto, Ottawa, Mississauga, Brampton, Hamilton, Markham, Vaughan, Richmond Hill, Barrie, London, Kitchener, Windsor, Oakville, Oshawa, Whitby, Burlington, Cambridge, Greater Sudbury. /ca/on/
- British Columbia — BC Hydro pays up to $4,000 for a heat pump that replaces electric heat. CleanBC pays more for income-qualified homes. 18 cities, including Abbotsford, Burnaby, Chilliwack, Coquitlam, Fort St. John, Kamloops, Kelowna, Langley, Maple Ridge, Nanaimo, Penticton, Prince George, Richmond, Squamish, Surrey, Vancouver, Vernon, Victoria. /ca/bc/
- Alberta — Programs depend on your city and utility. We show only what is open. 6 cities, including Calgary, Edmonton, Red Deer, Lethbridge, St. Albert. /ca/ab/
- Nova Scotia — Efficiency Nova Scotia pays per ton through a home energy assessment, up to $5,000. 2 cities, including Halifax. /ca/ns/
- Newfoundland and Labrador — Up to $22,000 to switch from oil to a heat pump, plus takeCHARGE insulation rebates. 5 cities, including St. John's, Mount Pearl, Paradise, Corner Brook, Labrador City. /ca/nl/
- Prince Edward Island — The heat pump rebate ended April 15, 2026. Free insulation and insulation rebates are still open. 2 cities, including Charlottetown, Summerside. /ca/pe/
- New Brunswick — NB Power pays $1,500 for a central heat pump and $550 for a heat pump water heater. 2 cities, including Moncton, Fredericton. /ca/nb/
- Canada (federal) — National Heat Pump Rebate announced Oct 8, 2026: up to $10,000 below the median income, $2,000 otherwise, launch expected early 2027, eligibility rules not yet published. /programs/national-heat-pump-rebate/ and guides at /blog/should-you-wait-federal-heat-pump-rebate/, /blog/federal-heat-pump-rebate-stacking-by-province/

**United States**
- California — Most statewide programs are closed. Your utility, such as SMUD, LADWP or a city utility, decides what is open. 24 cities, including Los Angeles, Sacramento, Bay Area, San Diego, Inland Empire. /us/ca/
- Massachusetts — Mass Save rebates, often paid to your installer. 41 towns with their own utilities are left out. 13 cities, including Boston, Worcester, Springfield, Cambridge, Lowell, Brockton, New Bedford, Quincy, Lynn, Fall River, Newton, Somerville. /us/ma/
- New York — NYS Clean Heat through your utility: Con Edison, National Grid, NYSEG, Central Hudson and more. 21 cities, including New York City, Yonkers, Mount Vernon, New Rochelle, White Plains, Brookhaven, Islip, Babylon, Huntington, Smithtown, Oyster Bay, Southampton, Poughkeepsie, Newburgh, Kingston, Beacon, Saugerties, Albany, Buffalo, Rochester, Syracuse. /us/ny/
- Pennsylvania — Rebates depend on your utility: PECO, PPL, Duquesne or FirstEnergy. 4 cities, including Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Allentown, Erie. /us/pa/
- Colorado — Xcel Energy plus city utilities such as Fort Collins and Colorado Springs. 5 cities, including Denver, Colorado Springs, Aurora, Fort Collins, Boulder. /us/co/
- Vermont — Efficiency Vermont and your electric company, such as Green Mountain Power. 5 cities, including Burlington, South Burlington, Rutland, Barre, Montpelier. /us/vt/
- Michigan — DTE and Consumers Energy rebates, plus free weatherization for income-qualified homes. 4 cities, including Detroit, Grand Rapids, Ann Arbor, Lansing. /us/mi/
- New Jersey — PSE&G, JCP&L and Atlantic City Electric programs, plus the New Jersey Clean Energy Program. 4 cities, including Newark, Jersey City, Toms River, Atlantic City. /us/nj/
- Illinois — ComEd, Nicor Gas, Peoples Gas and Ameren Illinois programs, plus Illinois Shines for solar. 4 cities, including Chicago, Aurora, Naperville, Peoria. /us/il/
- Washington — Puget Sound Energy, Seattle City Light, Avista, Tacoma Power and Clark Public Utilities programs. 5 cities, including Seattle, Spokane, Tacoma, Vancouver, Bellevue. /us/wa/
- Minnesota — Xcel Energy, CenterPoint Energy and Minnesota Power programs, plus Save Energy Minnesota. 4 cities, including Minneapolis, Saint Paul, Rochester, Duluth. /us/mn/

Note: as of 2026, the federal 25C/25D tax credits expired for US installs after December 31, 2025 (OBBBA). We reflect this on every US page rather than assuming they still apply.

## Key tools

- Free 20-second assessment: homepage widget estimates a household's rebate total by province/state and (where applicable) heating type and income tier
- PowerScore leaderboard: /powerscore/ — ranks every covered city 0-100 on rebate generosity and accessibility
- Stacking Calculator: /stacking-calculator/ — shows how multiple category rebates combine for one home, per city
- Installer directory: /installers/ — region-first drill-down to real local installers by city and category, with Google ratings and review counts
- Retrofit Assessment: /retrofit-assessment/ — fuller intake for a personalized rebate + installer match

## How the installer directory works

We are an independent directory, not an exclusive-lead broker. Installers are sourced from Google Places (name, rating, review count, and — where recoverable — contact email), verified as real local businesses. Homeowners browse and choose their own installer; we do not sell one homeowner's contact info to multiple installers, and we do not fabricate installer reviews, quotes, or testimonials.

## Content

- Blog and guides: /blog/, /guides/ — rebate program explainers, equipment comparisons (heat pump vs. furnace, battery brands), retrofit sequencing
- Rebate questions: /questions/ — direct answers to common homeowner questions
- Share Your Cost: /share-your-cost/ — real homeowner-submitted rebate totals, not manufactured testimonials

## About this service

HomePowerRebate is an independent service, not affiliated with any government, utility, or installer. We do not sell homeowner data to multiple installers. Program figures are sourced from official government/utility program pages and cited on the relevant page; where a program has closed or changed, we say so rather than showing an outdated number.
